content.prompt: Use Pythagoras’ theorem to find the value of the pronumeral. Calculate your answer first as a square root and then correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Source 5, Q4a: 3 cm, 5 cm, $x$ cm; right angle at bl.
spec.mathematics: Source 5, Q4a: 3 cm, 5 cm, $x$ cm; right angle at bl.

answer.worked:
Using Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=3^2+5^2\\x^2&=34\\x&=\sqrt{34}\text{ cm}\\x&\approx5.83\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Source 5, Q4b: 4 cm, 8 cm, $y$ cm; right angle at tl.
spec.mathematics: Source 5, Q4b: 4 cm, 8 cm, $y$ cm; right angle at tl.

answer.worked:
Using Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}y^2&=4^2+8^2\\y^2&=80\\y&=\sqrt{80}\text{ cm}\\y&\approx8.94\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Source 5, Q4c: $x$ cm, 2 cm, 7 cm; right angle at br.
spec.mathematics: Source 5, Q4c: $x$ cm, 2 cm, 7 cm; right angle at br.

answer.worked:
Using Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+2^2&=7^2\\x^2&=7^2-2^2\\x^2&=45\\x&=\sqrt{45}\text{ cm}\\x&\approx6.71\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Source 5, Q4d: 7 cm, $y$ cm, 11 cm; right angle at tl.
spec.mathematics: Source 5, Q4d: 7 cm, $y$ cm, 11 cm; right angle at tl.

answer.worked:
Using Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}y^2+7^2&=11^2\\y^2&=11^2-7^2\\y^2&=72\\y&=\sqrt{72}\text{ cm}\\y&\approx8.49\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Source 5, Q4e: 18 cm, 4 cm, $a$ cm; right angle at tr.
spec.mathematics: Source 5, Q4e: 18 cm, 4 cm, $a$ cm; right angle at tr.

answer.worked:
Using Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}a^2&=18^2+4^2\\a^2&=340\\a&=\sqrt{340}\text{ cm}\\a&\approx18.44\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Source 5, Q4f: $b$ cm, 7 cm, 10 cm; right angle at bl.
spec.mathematics: Source 5, Q4f: $b$ cm, 7 cm, 10 cm; right angle at bl.

answer.worked:
Using Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}b^2+7^2&=10^2\\b^2&=10^2-7^2\\b^2&=51\\b&=\sqrt{51}\text{ cm}\\b&\approx7.14\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Source Q4g isosceles triangle; matching sloping-side ticks, dashed perpendicular altitude 7 cm, whole base 6 cm, sloping side x cm.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular from the apex bisects the base of the isosceles triangle, so each half is $3\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=7^2+3^2\\x^2&=58\\x&=\sqrt{58}\text{ cm}\\x&\approx7.62\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Source Q4h isosceles triangle; matching sloping-side ticks, dashed perpendicular altitude 6 cm, whole base y cm, sloping side 8 cm.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular from the apex bisects the base. Let each half be $z\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}z^2+6^2&=8^2\\z^2&=64-36\\z&=\sqrt{28}\text{ cm}\\y&=2\sqrt{28}\text{ cm}\\y&\approx10.58\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Correct to 2 decimal places.
